newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - Volvo set to win its battle of Britain.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Volvo set to win its battle of Britain.

text.p: Volvo Cars is set to win its battle of Britain and with a strong finish this year's sales will almost equal 1995 figures, Hans-Olov Olsson, Volvo's president of Europe marketing, told Reuters.
"We will win the battle of Britain. Right now we are making a big effort to boost sales and we aim to sell 38,000 cars in Britain in 1996," Olsson said in an interview on Tuesday.
While Volvo sales shrank in the expanding British market, Olsson said the Swedish group would end the year with a rise.
In January-August this year, sales in Great Britain fell some 20 percent to 21,160 cars. Sales were 39,600 in the whole of 1995.
One of the things hampering Volvo Cars this year has been the phasing out of the old 400-series and the introduction of the new S40/V40 in Britain.
Before replacement the 300- and 400-series accounted for 60 percent of sales in Britain and deliveries of the new series have been slow.
"We have a delivery backlog of 8,000 cars of the S40/V40 in Britain. But now the cars come in and sales will pick up this year and we will continue to raise sales next year," he said.

On the West European market Volvo Cars' sales have also slumped this year, by 13 percent to 130,113 for the first eight months. But Olsson is confident that the company will take back some of that loss before the year is over.
"Again the problem is our order backlog on the S40/V40. Our sales are even a few percent ahead of plan. I am sure that our sales will increase during the rest of the year," Olsson said.
